hints: Total opposing force up $BC$ combines friction and gravity component: $960 + 1200(10)(0.05) = 960 + 600 = 1560\text{ N}$.
At steady climbing speed $V$, driving force equals opposing force: $F = 1560\text{ N}$.
Calculate speed: $V = \frac{P}{F} = \frac{25200}{1560} = \frac{210}{13} \approx 16.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Total work done in $40\text{ s}$ at constant power is $W = P t = 25200 \times 40 = 1008000\text{ J} = 1008\text{ kJ}$.
State the opposing force in Newtons, speed in metres per second, and work in kilojoules.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the total opposing force along the incline $BC$:
$$F_{\text{oppose}} = R + mg\sin\theta = 960 + (1200)(10)(0.05) = 960 + 600 = 1560\text{ N}$$

Determine the new constant speed $V$ where driving force balances opposing load:
$$F = F_{\text{oppose}} = 1560\text{ N}$$
$$V = \frac{P}{F} = \frac{25200}{1560} = \frac{210}{13}\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 16.1538\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 16.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the total work done by the engine during $40\text{ s}$ on the incline:
$$W = P t = (25200)(40) = 1008000\text{ J} = 1008\text{ kJ} \quad (1.008\text{ MJ} \approx 1.01\text{ MJ})$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum opposing forces on hill:
- Resistance plus gravity component:
$$F_{\text{oppose}} = 960 + 600 = 1560\text{ N}$$

Find steady climbing velocity:
- Power over opposing load:
$$V = \frac{25200}{1560} = \frac{210}{13} \approx 16.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate energy delivered:
- Engine power over $40\text{ s}$:
$$W = 25200 \times 40 = 1008000\text{ J} = 1008\text{ kJ}$$
The engine expends $1008\text{ kJ}$ climbing the incline.
